raw_record.question_text: Express the ratio of $\tan V$ as a decimal to the nearest hundredth.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a right triangle with vertices V, W, X and a right-angle marker at W. The side lengths shown are WV = 72, WX = 21, and hypotenuse VX = 75. From the text, the goal is to express tan V as a decimal rounded to the nearest hundredth. For angle V, identify the opposite leg as WX = 21 and the adjacent leg as WV = 72. Use the tangent definition in a right triangle: tan(V) = opposite/adjacent = 21/72. Compute 21 ÷ 72 = 0.2916..., then round to the nearest hundredth to get 0.29.
